You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testExtremeValues` in `NormalDistributionTest` is testing extreme values for the cumulative probability calculation in `NormalDistributionImpl`. The test checks the lower and upper tails for a normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. It iterates over a range of values and asserts that the cumulative probabilities are within expected ranges.

Looking at the current bug report, it mentions a `ConvergenceException` in `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability()` for very large or small parameters, including Infinity and -Infinity. The test case itself includes a call to `cumulativeProbability(Double.MAX_VALUE)`, which could trigger this issue.

The test code iterates up to a maximum value and expects the cumulative probability to be 1 when the input is `Double.MAX_VALUE`. However, the calculation for very large values may lead to a `ConvergenceException` due to precision issues or convergence problems in the cumulative probability calculation.

To localize the fault further, we need to inspect the implementation of `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability` to understand how extreme values are handled in the calculation.

Next, we will retrieve the code snippet for `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability` to analyze its implementation in detail.

messages.content:
The `cumulativeProbability` method in `NormalDistributionImpl` calculates the cumulative probability using the error function (Erf) for a given input `x`. It appears that for extreme values where the `Erf.erf` calculation encounters convergence issues and throws `MaxIterationsExceededException`, it handles the situation by returning specific values based on whether `x` is beyond a certain range.

In the catch block for `MaxIterationsExceededException`, if `x` is beyond `(mean ± 20 * standardDeviation)`, it returns 0 or 1 respectively. This explains why the test case may face convergence exceptions for very large values such as `Double.MAX_VALUE`, as the method does not handle such extreme cases gracefully.

To address the convergence exceptions for very large or small input values in the `NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability` method, we should enhance the handling of extreme values within the convergence try-catch block.

Next, I will provide the best locations to fix this issue.
`org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.cumulativeProbability(double)`

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
